title: Research Collaborators
dek: Collaborate on focused projects in GNSS, urban positioning, atmospheric sensing, autonomous navigation, or navigation simulation.
body: This opportunity is for students and researchers interested in developing a focused research output, experiment, dataset, simulator, or working paper together.

Possible areas include urban and smartphone GNSS, multipath and NLOS, GNSS reflectometry, radio occultation, autonomous navigation, sensor fusion, and browser-based simulation. Project scope, authorship, responsibilities, and timelines will be agreed before work begins.
requirements: Reliable communication and the ability to agree on a realistic project scope and timeline.
Careful documentation of methods, sources, assumptions, code, and progress.
Respect for research ethics, data permissions, intellectual property, and accurate attribution.
Willingness to give and receive constructive feedback.
perks: Work on a clearly scoped GNSS or navigation research problem with flexible remote coordination.
Receive peer feedback on methods, code, analysis, visualisation, and technical writing.
Build a concrete research artifact such as an experiment, dataset note, simulator contribution, poster, or working-paper section.
Receive visible credit appropriate to your documented contribution; authorship is discussed using the agreed project scope and actual contributions.
fitIf: You are a student, independent researcher, developer, or early-career researcher who can take ownership of a bounded task.
You are curious about GNSS, positioning, atmospheric sensing, autonomous systems, or research software.
You can explain what you tried, what worked, what failed, and what evidence supports your conclusions.
You are comfortable learning unfamiliar technical material and asking focused questions.
preferred: Experience with Python, data analysis, scientific computing, geospatial data, signal processing, or technical writing.
Familiarity with GitHub, reproducible notebooks, research documentation, or collaborative code review.
Interest in smartphone GNSS, multipath and NLOS, GNSS-R, radio occultation, FORMOSAT/COSMIC data, UAV navigation, or sensor fusion.
A short example of previous work, coursework, code, writing, or a proposed research question. Relevant experience is helpful but not mandatory.
engagementNote: This is an independent, project-based research collaboration rather than an employment offer. Funding, expenses, deliverables, attribution, and any authorship expectations must be agreed in writing for each project before work begins.
